deterministic.name: check-verifier-contract.py
deterministic.evidence: Manual frozen-source/checklist review; private deterministic checker not executed. qc/runs/coldwater-2026-10-01-history-hardening-r3/per-row-review/evidence/deterministic/manual-facts.json shell_syntax shows .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-10-01-history-hardening-r3/task/tests/test.sh bash -n exit 0. .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-10-01-history-hardening-r3/task/tests/test.sh:60-61 initializes zero reward and EXIT trap; :68 checks /app/server.js; :48 and :112-119 probe liveness before :213/224 suites; :193 exports APP_RESTART_HELPER, wired at functional/judge.toml:18. Full configured verifier execution is absent; template restart helper liveness is not proven by source checks. Confirmed source defect in the frozen shared test.sh: lines 152-159 send SIGTERM to the old process group but continue after 5 seconds even if it still lives; lines 160-175 launch a replacement and accept any HTTP response on port 3000 without checking that the new process owns the listener. restart_mcp.py:23-46 then reports helper exit 0 as a successful restart. No private checker/actual exploit run was performed.
deterministic.counterexample: A submission server installs a SIGTERM handler that keeps serving on port 3000. The restart helper waits five seconds, starts a replacement that cannot bind, then its /api/health probe talks to the original server and reports restart success. Scored restart durability can pass without a process restart, and a compliant implementation could be judged against the wrong process.
deterministic.suggested_fix: Fix the shared template/runner restart helper: require the old process group to terminate, require the replacement PID to remain alive, and verify the new listener belongs to that replacement before reporting success; then rerun the configured verifier on a new frozen candidate.
